hints.title: Binary Branching Over Alphabetic Characters
hints.text: Digits remain unchanged, whereas each alphabetic letter can be toggled between lowercase and uppercase, creating two alternative branches per letter.

hints.title: Prefix Branch Extension Invariant
hints.text: Extending previously formed string prefixes with either the lowercase or uppercase variant of the current character explores all combinations recursively.

hints.title: Index Traversal Recursive Generation Procedure
hints.text: Define a recursive function taking current index and accumulated character list. If index equals string length, join the characters and add to results. If the character at index is a digit, recurse with index plus one. If it is a letter, branch once with its lowercase form and once with its uppercase form.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def letterCasePermutation(self, s: str) -> List[str]:
        res = []
        n = len(s)
        def backtrack(i: int, path: List[str]):
            if i == n:
                res.append("".join(path))
                return
            ch = s[i]
            if ch.isalpha():
                path.append(ch.lower())
                backtrack(i + 1, path)
                path.pop()
                path.append(ch.upper())
                backtrack(i + 1, path)
                path.pop()
            else:
                path.append(ch)
                backtrack(i + 1, path)
                path.pop()

        backtrack(0, [])
        return res
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N * 2^L) time and O(N * 2^L) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating redundant permutations or duplicating full strings repeatedly creates large memory overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: With L letters, there are exactly 2^L valid output strings, each taking O(N) time to construct, leading to O(N * 2^L) time and space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize the binary tree branching structure and distinguish digits from letters.
